tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	#ifndef DSM_STORE_H
2	#define DSM_STORE_H
3	
4	#include "common/record.h"
5	
6	#include <stddef.h>
7	#include <stdint.h>
8	
9	/* A store file is one header followed by records, back to back:
10	 *
11	 *   [ header: 24 bytes ][ record 0: 48 ][ record 1: 48 ] ...
12	 *
13	 * Records are only ever added at the end. Nothing is rewritten in place.
14	 *
15	 * Crash recovery: store_open() checks every record of an existing file and
16	 * cuts the file off at the first one that is incomplete or damaged, which is
17	 * what a crash in the middle of a write leaves behind. store_get_recovery()
18	 * says what it kept and what it cut.
19	 *
20	 * Durability today: store_append() hands the bytes to the kernel. It does
21	 * not wait for them to reach the SD card (no fsync), so a power cut can
22	 * still lose the most recent records. */
23	
24	#define DSM_STORE_MAGIC "DSKY"
25	
26	/* The first 24 bytes of every store file. */
27	struct dsm_store_header {
28	    char     magic[4];         /* "DSKY", no terminating zero */
29	    uint16_t schema_ver;       /* DSM_SCHEMA_VER of the records inside */
30	    uint16_t record_size;      /* sizeof(struct dsm_record) */
31	    uint64_t created_real_ns;  /* CLOCK_REALTIME when the file was made */
32	    uint32_t reserved;         /* always 0; puts crc32 last with no padding */
33	    uint32_t crc32;            /* covers every byte before this field */
34	};
35	
36	_Static_assert(sizeof(struct dsm_store_header) == 24,
37	               "dsm_store_header must be exactly 24 bytes");
38	_Static_assert(offsetof(struct dsm_store_header, crc32) == 20,
39	               "crc32 must be the last 4 bytes of the header");
40	
41	enum store_status {
42	    STORE_OK = 0,
43	    STORE_ERR_IO,      /* a system call failed; errno says why */
44	    STORE_ERR_FORMAT,  /* the file exists but is not a store file; untouched */
45	    STORE_ERR_BADREC,  /* the record's CRC does not match; nothing written */
46	    STORE_ERR_BROKEN,  /* an earlier write failed; no more appends */
47	};
48	
49	/* What recovery did when the file was opened. Both are 0 for a new file. */
50	struct store_recovery {
51	    uint64_t kept;       /* intact records found */
52	    uint64_t cut_bytes;  /* bytes cut off the end; 0 if the file was clean */
53	};
54	
55	/* Opaque: only store.c can see inside. */
56	struct dsm_store;
57	
58	enum store_status store_open(const char *path, struct dsm_store **out);
59	enum store_status store_append(struct dsm_store *s, const struct dsm_record *r);
60	enum store_status store_close(struct dsm_store *s);
61	struct store_recovery store_get_recovery(const struct dsm_store *s);

# term-project (Dark Sky Monitor) — CS 370
# Every target does what its name says. CLAUDE.md treats a lying target as a bug.

CC := gcc

# _POSIX_C_SOURCE: with -std=c17, the Pi's glibc hides fsync, ftruncate, pread
# and clock_gettime unless this is defined, and -Werror then fails the build.
# macOS shows them anyway, so leaving this out would only break on the Pi.
CFLAGS := -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O1 -Isrc -Itests \
          -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L
# -fno-sanitize-recover: undefined behavior stops the run instead of printing
# a message and carrying on, so `make asan` fails on it like it does on ASan.
SANFLAGS := -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer

# Portable library code (no main), built and tested on macOS and Linux.
# Each side adds files only to its own section (docs/m3-plan.md).

# --- shared (src/common) ---
COMMON_SRC  := src/common/crc32.c src/common/record.c src/common/log.c
COMMON_TSRC := tests/test_crc32.c tests/test_record.c tests/test_log.c
COMMON_HDR  := src/common/crc32.h src/common/record.h src/common/log.h

# --- storage side (src/store, src/dsq) ---
STORE_SRC  := src/store/store.c
STORE_TSRC := tests/test_store.c
STORE_HDR  := src/store/store.h

# --- sensor side (src/sensors; portable parts only) ---
SENSOR_SRC  := src/sensors/convert.c
SENSOR_TSRC := tests/test_convert.c
SENSOR_HDR  := src/sensors/convert.h

SRC  := $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) $(SENSOR_SRC)
TSRC := tests/test_main.c $(COMMON_TSRC) $(STORE_TSRC) $(SENSOR_TSRC)
HDR  := tests/check.h tests/suites.h $(COMMON_HDR) $(STORE_HDR) $(SENSOR_HDR)

TESTBIN := build/test_all

## all: build the test binary
all: $(TESTBIN)

$(TESTBIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) $(HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) $(TSRC) -o $@

## test: run every test suite
test: $(TESTBIN)
	./$(TESTBIN)

## asan: rebuild with AddressSanitizer + UBSan and run the tests
asan: CFLAGS += $(SANFLAGS)
asan: clean test

## memcheck: run the tests under valgrind (Linux/Pi only, not on macOS)
memcheck: all
	@if ! command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "make memcheck: valgrind not installed here (expected on macOS - run this on the Pi)."; \
	  else \
	    valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 ./$(TESTBIN); \
	  fi

## soakcheck: 1-hour miniature of the graded 48h soak
soakcheck:
	@echo "make soakcheck: not implemented yet - needs the supervisor and heartbeat logging."
	@echo "Per spec 3.4 this must exercise: startup, hourly heartbeat (liveness/RSS/event counts),"
	@echo "an injected fault with detect-degrade-recover, and an orderly shutdown."

## deploy: rsync the tree to the Pi. usage: make deploy PI=pi@hostname
deploy:
	@if [ -z "$(PI)" ]; then \
	    echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@hostname"; exit 1; \
	  else \
	    rsync -av --exclude '.git' --exclude 'build' --exclude 'transcripts' ./ $(PI):~/term-project/; \
	  fi

## clean: remove build artifacts
clean:
	rm -rf build

## help: list targets
help:
	@grep -E '^## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sed 's/^## /  /'

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck deploy clean help

content.text:
Commit 1 is done: `d6ddff7 M3: store_sync and write/fsync counters`. It's local only; I'll push after commit 3, as you said.

I didn't have the approved plan in this session, so I took it from your earlier session (`58a1c11a`) and am following its commit list.

**What changed**
- **`store_sync()`** ([store.c:192](src/store/store.c#L192)) calls `fsync`. It returns BROKEN on a broken handle. If `fsync` fails, it marks the handle broken and returns IO, and it never retries.
- **`store_close()`** now syncs before closing. If the sync fails, it still closes and frees the handle and returns the sync's error. On a broken handle it skips the sync, closes and frees, and returns BROKEN.
- **`store_counters { records, writes, fsyncs }`** counts what this handle has done since `store_open()`. Refused records and failed writes aren't counted, and recovery's own `fsync` isn't either.
- **The header comment** now states the durability rule: a power cut loses at most what was appended since the last `store_sync()`. The library has no clock; `stored` decides how often to sync.

**Tests**
- I added the tests first, with do-nothing stubs. 8 checks failed, each because the behavior was missing. With the real code: `make test` 425 checks, 0 failed; `make asan` 425, 0 failed; `make memcheck` 0 errors, 0 bytes in use at exit.
- `test_counters` covers appends, a refused record, two syncs and a reopen.
- `test_sync_on_broken_handle` makes a write really fail using the `RLIMIT_FSIZE` trick from Nick's test. Sync and close then return BROKEN, and reopening keeps 1 record and cuts the partial one.
- **Not unit-tested:**
  - **Whether `store_close` actually calls `fsync`:** the file contents look the same either way. I checked it once with strace instead: the whole suite made 5 `fsync` calls before this change and 33 after.
  - **A failing `fsync`:** I can't make one fail without faking `fsync` itself.

**Likely defense question:** *"`fsync` failed. Why not just call it again?"*

On Linux, a failed `fsync` can mark the pages it couldn't write as clean (the 2018 PostgreSQL "fsyncgate" case). A second `fsync` then reports success for data that never reached the card. So the only honest response is to stop trusting the handle: `stored` exits with code 2, and recovery on the next open works out what is really in the file. A follow-up you may get: *"So what's your worst-case data loss?"* Everything appended since the last successful sync. With `stored` syncing every 60 s, that's at most 60 s of records.

# Every target does what its name says. CLAUDE.md treats a lying target as a bug.

CC := gcc

# _POSIX_C_SOURCE: with -std=c17, the Pi's glibc hides fsync, ftruncate, pread
# and clock_gettime unless this is defined, and -Werror then fails the build.
# macOS shows them anyway, so leaving this out would only break on the Pi.
CFLAGS := -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O1 -Isrc -Itests \
          -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L
# -fno-sanitize-recover: undefined behavior stops the run instead of printing
# a message and carrying on, so `make asan` fails on it like it does on ASan.
SANFLAGS := -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer

$(TESTBIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) $(HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) $(TSRC) -o $@

build/stored: $(STORED_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) $(COMMON_HDR) $(STORE_HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(STORED_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) -o $@

build/itest_stored: $(STORE_ITSRC) $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(COMMON_HDR) \
                    $(STORE_HDR) $(STORE_CLIENT_HDR) tests/check.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(STORE_ITSRC) $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) -o $@

## test: run every test suite
test: $(TESTBIN)
	./$(TESTBIN)

## itest: run the real stored and talk to it over its socket (Linux only)
ifeq ($(UNAME),Linux)
itest: build/stored build/itest_stored
	./build/itest_stored ./build/stored
else
itest:
	@echo "make itest: needs Linux (macOS has no SOCK_SEQPACKET) - run this on the Pi."
endif

## asan: rebuild with AddressSanitizer + UBSan and run the tests (and itest on Linux)
asan: CFLAGS += $(SANFLAGS)
asan: clean test $(LINUX_TEST)

## memcheck: run the tests (and itest, with stored traced too) under valgrind (Linux/Pi only)
memcheck: all
	@if ! command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "make memcheck: valgrind not installed here (expected on macOS - run this on the Pi)."; \
	  else \
	    valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 ./$(TESTBIN) && \
	    if [ -n "$(LINUX_BIN)" ]; then \
	      valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 \
	        --trace-children=yes --child-silent-after-fork=yes \
	        ./build/itest_stored ./build/stored; \
	    fi; \
	  fi

content.text:
Commit 1 of 3 is pushed: `8f93e45 M3: stored daemon, store_client, directory fsync, make itest`. `d6ddff7` (`store_sync` and the counters) went up with it.

**What's in it**
- **Directory fsync:** `store_open` now fsyncs a new file's header and then its parent directory ([store.c:116](src/store/store.c#L116)). It does this on every open, not only on create. Otherwise a crash between creating the file and syncing the directory leaves a 24-byte file that later opens treat as old and never sync.
- **`stored`** ([stored.c](src/store/stored.c)) follows S3, with these additions:
  - The poll timeout is capped at 1 s.
  - On SIGTERM it reads in everything clients already sent, including connections not accepted yet, so a clean stop loses nothing.
  - It refuses to delete anything at the socket path that isn't a socket.
  - An optional third argument sets the sync interval in seconds (default 60). The itest uses 1 to check the sync line.
- **`store_client`** ([store_client.c](src/store/store_client.c)):
  - It never blocks: if `stored` is down or its queue is full, the record is dropped and counted.
  - It tries to reconnect at most once per second.
  - It logs only state changes (connected, disconnected, queue full), not every dropped record.
- **Makefile:**
  - On Linux, `make all` now also builds `build/stored` and `build/itest_stored`.
  - `make asan` also runs the itest.
  - `make memcheck` also runs the itest under valgrind, with `stored` itself traced.

**Evidence**
- I wrote the tests first:
  - The directory-fsync unit test failed (`store_open` succeeded in a directory it couldn't sync).
  - The itest failed 63 of 81 checks with no `stored` binary.
- With the code in place:
  - `make test`: 429 checks, 0 failed.
  - `make itest`: 137 checks, 0 failed, and it passed 10 repeat runs.
  - `make asan`: both suites pass.
  - `make clean && make memcheck`: 0 errors and 0 bytes in use at exit for both binaries. `ps` showed `stored` running under valgrind during the itest.

**Not covered:** `stored`'s exit 2 after a failed write or fsync has no itest case. The library tests cover the broken-handle behavior, but nothing makes `stored` itself hit it.

**For Nick (this goes in the progress log in commit 3):**
- Socket paths must be under 108 bytes. `~/dsm/run/stored.sock` is fine.
- His sensor programs will log `store_connect`, `store_disconnect` and `store_full` lines under their own program names.
- After `make asan`, `make memcheck` still needs a `make clean` first. That's the existing shared-`build/` bug.

**Likely defense questions**
1. *"`stored` gets SIGTERM while 30 records are sitting in its socket queue. What happens to them?"* They're stored. Each of those `send()` calls succeeded, so the client counts the record as delivered. After the signal, `stored` accepts any pending connections and reads up to 1024 messages per client before closing. `test_two_clients_clean_stop` sends SIGTERM immediately after 50 sends and finds all 50 in the file. After `kill -9`, those queued records are lost, and nothing counts them: that is the seq-gap note.
2. *"Your signal handler only sets a flag. What if the signal arrives between checking the flag and calling `poll()`?"* `poll()` would sleep through it. That's why the timeout is capped at 1 s: the worst case is a 1 s delay, not 60 s. (The textbook fix is `ppoll` with the signal blocked; the cap is simpler and also gives `dskyd` a once-a-second loop at M4.)
3. *"Why does `fsync` on the file not make a new file durable?"* The file's name is an entry in its directory, and that entry is the directory's data, not the file's. Without syncing the directory, a power cut can leave a fully synced file with no name pointing to it.

Starting commit 2 (`store_scan` + `dsq dump`) next.

# term-project (Dark Sky Monitor) — CS 370
# Every target does what its name says. CLAUDE.md treats a lying target as a bug.

CC := gcc

# _POSIX_C_SOURCE: with -std=c17, the Pi's glibc hides fsync, ftruncate, pread
# and clock_gettime unless this is defined, and -Werror then fails the build.
# macOS shows them anyway, so leaving this out would only break on the Pi.
CFLAGS := -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O1 -Isrc -Itests \
          -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L
# -fno-sanitize-recover: undefined behavior stops the run instead of printing
# a message and carrying on, so `make asan` fails on it like it does on ASan.
SANFLAGS := -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer

# Portable library code (no main), built and tested on macOS and Linux.
# Each side adds files only to its own section (docs/m3-plan.md).

# --- shared (src/common) ---
COMMON_SRC  := src/common/crc32.c src/common/record.c src/common/log.c
COMMON_TSRC := tests/test_crc32.c tests/test_record.c tests/test_log.c
COMMON_HDR  := src/common/crc32.h src/common/record.h src/common/log.h

# --- storage side (src/store, src/dsq) ---
STORE_SRC  := src/store/store.c
STORE_TSRC := tests/test_store.c
STORE_HDR  := src/store/store.h
# Linux only (SOCK_SEQPACKET). Sensor programs link STORE_CLIENT_SRC.
STORE_CLIENT_SRC := src/store/store_client.c
STORE_CLIENT_HDR := src/store/store_client.h
STORED_SRC       := src/store/stored.c
STORE_ITSRC      := tests/itest_stored.c

# --- sensor side (src/sensors; portable parts only) ---
SENSOR_SRC  := src/sensors/convert.c
SENSOR_TSRC := tests/test_convert.c
SENSOR_HDR  := src/sensors/convert.h

SRC  := $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) $(SENSOR_SRC)
TSRC := tests/test_main.c $(COMMON_TSRC) $(STORE_TSRC) $(SENSOR_TSRC)
HDR  := tests/check.h tests/suites.h $(COMMON_HDR) $(STORE_HDR) $(SENSOR_HDR)

TESTBIN := build/test_all

# Programs that need Linux: built, run under asan and valgrind only there.
UNAME := $(shell uname -s)
ifeq ($(UNAME),Linux)
LINUX_BIN  := build/stored build/itest_stored
LINUX_TEST := itest
endif

## all: build the test binary (and stored + its integration test on Linux)
all: $(TESTBIN) $(LINUX_BIN)

$(TESTBIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) $(HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) $(TSRC) -o $@

build/stored: $(STORED_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) $(COMMON_HDR) $(STORE_HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(STORED_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) -o $@

build/itest_stored: $(STORE_ITSRC) $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(COMMON_HDR) \
                    $(STORE_HDR) $(STORE_CLIENT_HDR) tests/check.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(STORE_ITSRC) $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) -o $@

## test: run every test suite
test: $(TESTBIN)
	./$(TESTBIN)

## itest: run the real stored and talk to it over its socket (Linux only)
ifeq ($(UNAME),Linux)
itest: build/stored build/itest_stored
	./build/itest_stored ./build/stored
else
itest:
	@echo "make itest: needs Linux (macOS has no SOCK_SEQPACKET) - run this on the Pi."
endif

## asan: rebuild with AddressSanitizer + UBSan and run the tests (and itest on Linux)
asan: CFLAGS += $(SANFLAGS)
asan: clean test $(LINUX_TEST)

## memcheck: run the tests (and itest, with stored traced too) under valgrind (Linux/Pi only)
memcheck: all
	@if ! command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "make memcheck: valgrind not installed here (expected on macOS - run this on the Pi)."; \
	  else \
	    valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 ./$(TESTBIN) && \
	    if [ -n "$(LINUX_BIN)" ]; then \
	      valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 \
	        --trace-children=yes --child-silent-after-fork=yes \
	        ./build/itest_stored ./build/stored; \
	    fi; \
	  fi

## soakcheck: 1-hour miniature of the graded 48h soak
soakcheck:
	@echo "make soakcheck: not implemented yet - needs the supervisor and heartbeat logging."
	@echo "Per spec 3.4 this must exercise: startup, hourly heartbeat (liveness/RSS/event counts),"
	@echo "an injected fault with detect-degrade-recover, and an orderly shutdown."

## deploy: rsync the tree to the Pi. usage: make deploy PI=pi@hostname
deploy:
	@if [ -z "$(PI)" ]; then \
	    echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@hostname"; exit 1; \
	  else \
	    rsync -av --exclude '.git' --exclude 'build' --exclude 'transcripts' ./ $(PI):~/term-project/; \
	  fi

## clean: remove build artifacts
clean:
	rm -rf build

## help: list targets
help:
	@grep -E '^## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sed 's/^## /  /'

.PHONY: all test itest asan memcheck soakcheck deploy clean help

# term-project (Dark Sky Monitor) — CS 370
# Every target does what its name says. CLAUDE.md treats a lying target as a bug.

CC := gcc

# _POSIX_C_SOURCE: with -std=c17, the Pi's glibc hides fsync, ftruncate, pread
# and clock_gettime unless this is defined, and -Werror then fails the build.
# macOS shows them anyway, so leaving this out would only break on the Pi.
CFLAGS := -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O1 -Isrc -Itests \
          -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L
# -fno-sanitize-recover: undefined behavior stops the run instead of printing
# a message and carrying on, so `make asan` fails on it like it does on ASan.
SANFLAGS := -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer

# Portable library code (no main), built and tested on macOS and Linux.
# Each side adds files only to its own section (docs/m3-plan.md).

# --- shared (src/common) ---
COMMON_SRC  := src/common/crc32.c src/common/record.c src/common/log.c
COMMON_TSRC := tests/test_crc32.c tests/test_record.c tests/test_log.c
COMMON_HDR  := src/common/crc32.h src/common/record.h src/common/log.h

# --- storage side (src/store, src/dsq) ---
STORE_SRC  := src/store/store.c src/dsq/dump.c
STORE_TSRC := tests/test_store.c tests/test_dsq.c
STORE_HDR  := src/store/store.h src/dsq/dump.h
DSQ_SRC    := src/dsq/dsq.c
# Linux only (SOCK_SEQPACKET). Sensor programs link STORE_CLIENT_SRC.
STORE_CLIENT_SRC := src/store/store_client.c
STORE_CLIENT_HDR := src/store/store_client.h
STORED_SRC       := src/store/stored.c
STORE_ITSRC      := tests/itest_stored.c

# --- sensor side (src/sensors; portable parts only) ---
SENSOR_SRC  := src/sensors/convert.c
SENSOR_TSRC := tests/test_convert.c
SENSOR_HDR  := src/sensors/convert.h

SRC  := $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) $(SENSOR_SRC)
TSRC := tests/test_main.c $(COMMON_TSRC) $(STORE_TSRC) $(SENSOR_TSRC)
HDR  := tests/check.h tests/suites.h $(COMMON_HDR) $(STORE_HDR) $(SENSOR_HDR)

TESTBIN := build/test_all

# Programs that need Linux: built, run under asan and valgrind only there.
UNAME := $(shell uname -s)
ifeq ($(UNAME),Linux)
LINUX_BIN  := build/stored build/itest_stored
LINUX_TEST := itest
endif

## all: build the test binary (and stored + its integration test on Linux)
all: $(TESTBIN) $(LINUX_BIN)

$(TESTBIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) $(HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) $(TSRC) -o $@

build/stored: $(STORED_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) $(COMMON_HDR) $(STORE_HDR)
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(STORED_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(STORE_SRC) -o $@

build/itest_stored: $(STORE_ITSRC) $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) $(COMMON_HDR) \
                    $(STORE_HDR) $(STORE_CLIENT_HDR) tests/check.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(STORE_ITSRC) $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) -o $@

## test: run every test suite
test: $(TESTBIN)
	./$(TESTBIN)

## itest: run the real stored and talk to it over its socket (Linux only)
ifeq ($(UNAME),Linux)
itest: build/stored build/itest_stored
	./build/itest_stored ./build/stored
else
itest:
	@echo "make itest: needs Linux (macOS has no SOCK_SEQPACKET) - run this on the Pi."
endif

## asan: rebuild with AddressSanitizer + UBSan and run the tests (and itest on Linux)
asan: CFLAGS += $(SANFLAGS)
asan: clean test $(LINUX_TEST)

## memcheck: run the tests (and itest, with stored traced too) under valgrind (Linux/Pi only)
memcheck: all
	@if ! command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "make memcheck: valgrind not installed here (expected on macOS - run this on the Pi)."; \
	  else \
	    valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 ./$(TESTBIN) && \
	    if [ -n "$(LINUX_BIN)" ]; then \
	      valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1 \
	        --trace-children=yes --child-silent-after-fork=yes \
	        ./build/itest_stored ./build/stored; \
	    fi; \
	  fi

## soakcheck: 1-hour miniature of the graded 48h soak

	@echo "make soakcheck: not implemented yet - needs the supervisor and heartbeat logging."
	@echo "Per spec 3.4 this must exercise: startup, hourly heartbeat (liveness/RSS/event counts),"
	@echo "an injected fault with detect-degrade-recover, and an orderly shutdown."

	    echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@hostname"; exit 1; \
	  else \
	    rsync -av --exclude '.git' --exclude 'build' --exclude 'transcripts' ./ $(PI):~/term-project/; \
	  fi

## clean: remove build artifacts
clean:
	rm -rf build

## help: list targets
help:
	@grep -E '^## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sed 's/^## /  /'

.PHONY: all test itest asan memcheck soakcheck deploy clean help

1. *"Is it safe to run `dsq` while `stored` is writing?"* Yes. It opens the file `O_RDONLY` and never truncates. It sees the file as it was when the scan began; a record `stored` is in the middle of writing just shows up as a few tail bytes. Only `stored`, through `recover()` at open, ever cuts the file.

  pass; `make clean && make memcheck` 0 errors, 0 bytes in use, for `test_all` and for
  `itest_stored` with `stored` traced. Tests were written first and seen failing each time.
- **Not yet verified:** any of it on `darksky.local` (step 1 of the integration run).

### Build targets (confirmed with Nick)

| Target | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `build/dsq` | `dsq dump` | `make all`, macOS and Linux |
| `build/stored` | the daemon | `make all`, Linux only |
| `build/itest_stored` | integration test | `make all`, Linux only |
| `make itest` | runs `./build/itest_stored ./build/stored` | Linux; prints "needs Linux" on macOS |

- `make asan` now also runs `itest` on Linux; `make memcheck` also runs it under valgrind with
  `--trace-children=yes`, so `stored` itself is checked.
- **`STORE_CLIENT_SRC`** (`src/store/store_client.c`) is the variable for the sensor programs'
  link lines, for example
  `$(CC) $(CFLAGS) src/sensors/skyd.c ... $(STORE_CLIENT_SRC) $(COMMON_SRC) -o build/skyd`.
  The client needs only `src/common/` (record, CRC, logger), not the store library.
- `dsq`'s formatting is in `DSQ_LIB` (`src/dsq/dump.c`), so the test binary and `build/dsq`
  share it; `stored` does not link it.
- Known, unchanged: after `make asan`, run `make clean` before `make memcheck` (both build into
  `build/`, so memcheck would otherwise run the ASan binaries).

### How to run it (for N4 / `tools/run-m3.sh`)

```sh
mkdir -p ~/dsm/data ~/dsm/run
./build/stored ~/dsm/data/seg-000001.dsm ~/dsm/run/stored.sock 2>> ~/dsm/run/stored.log &
# then the sensor programs, each given ~/dsm/run/stored.sock
./build/dsq dump ~/dsm/data/seg-000001.dsm -n 20
kill -TERM <stored pid>      # exit 0: drained, synced, socket removed
```

- `stored <data-file> <socket-path> [sync-seconds]`. The third argument is optional (default
  60, 1–3600); the itest uses 1. Exit **0** stopped by SIGTERM/SIGINT; **1** bad arguments, a
  file that isn't a store file, or the socket can't be set up (including a non-socket file at
  the socket path, which it refuses to delete); **2** a write or `fsync` failed.
- Log lines (stderr): `INFO start file=.. kept=.. sync_s=..`; `WARN recover kept=N
  cut_bytes=K` when recovery cut anything; `INFO sync records=.. bad=.. clients=.. fsyncs=..`
  every sync; `WARN bad_message len=..`, `WARN bad_record source=.. seq=..`; `INFO stop
  records=..`. Every start appends a START record from source 6 (`stored`).
- **Socket paths must be shorter than 108 bytes** (`sun_path`). `~/dsm/run/stored.sock` is fine.
- `store_client_send()` never blocks (`O_NONBLOCK`, `MSG_NOSIGNAL`): with `stored` down or
  behind it returns -1 and counts the drop; it retries the connection at most once per second.
  It logs only changes of state, under the sensor program's own name: `store_connect`,
  `store_connect_fail`, `store_disconnect`, `store_full`. Call `log_init()` before using it.
- On SIGTERM `stored` reads in whatever clients already sent (up to 1024 per client) before
  closing, so a clean stop loses no record whose `send()` succeeded.

### Note for the D demo write-up (`docs/m3-checkpoint.md`)

- **`kill -9 stored` leaves an expected `seq` gap.** Records already in the socket queue when it
  dies are lost, and `store_client_dropped()` does not count them: their `send()` succeeded. The
  next send after the kill fails (`EPIPE`) and is counted, and so is every send until the
  reconnect. So "no `seq` gaps" holds for the clean run (step 2), not across the kill (step 3).
  `itest` case "client through restart" shows the gap: seq 1–4 missing between two STARTs.
- **Directory `fsync`** runs on every `store_open()`, not only when the file is new: a crash
  between creating the file and syncing its directory would otherwise leave a file that looks
  old on the next start, with its name still not on the card.

### Open

- `stored`'s exit 2 (failed write or `fsync`) is covered only at the library level
  (`test_sync_on_broken_handle`); no itest case makes the daemon hit it.
- Nothing stops two `stored`s on the same data file; at M4 `dskyd` is the only launcher. An
  `fcntl` lock in `store_open()` would close it if wanted.
- `DESIGN.md` note on the M3 slice and SEQPACKET being Linux-only (Nick's close-out item).
- Cross-review: Liam's review of Nick's sensor code in `PROMPTLOG-liam.md`, once N3 is pushed.

### How to run it (for N4 / `tools/run-m3.sh`)

```sh
mkdir -p ~/dsm/data ~/dsm/run
./build/stored ~/dsm/data/seg-000001.dsm ~/dsm/run/stored.sock 2>> ~/dsm/run/stored.log &
# then the sensor programs, each given ~/dsm/run/stored.sock
./build/dsq dump ~/dsm/data/seg-000001.dsm -n 20

```

  60, 1–3600); the itest uses 1. Exit **0** stopped by SIGTERM/SIGINT; **1** bad arguments, a
  file that isn't a store file, or the socket can't be set up (including a non-socket file at
  the socket path, which it refuses to delete); **2** a write or `fsync` failed.

  cut_bytes=K` when recovery cut anything; `INFO sync records=.. bad=.. clients=.. fsyncs=..`
  every sync; `WARN bad_message len=..`, `WARN bad_record source=.. seq=..`; `INFO stop
  records=..`. Every start appends a START record from source 6 (`stored`).

- `store_client_send()` never blocks (`O_NONBLOCK`, `MSG_NOSIGNAL`): with `stored` down or
  behind it returns -1 and counts the drop; it retries the connection at most once per second.
  It logs only changes of state, under the sensor program's own name: `store_connect`,
  `store_connect_fail`, `store_disconnect`, `store_full`. Call `log_init()` before using it.
- On SIGTERM `stored` reads in whatever clients already sent (up to 1024 per client) before
  closing, so a clean stop loses no record whose `send()` succeeded.

### Note for the D demo write-up (`docs/m3-checkpoint.md`)

- **`kill -9 stored` leaves an expected `seq` gap.** Records already in the socket queue when it
  dies are lost, and `store_client_dropped()` does not count them: their `send()` succeeded. The
  next send after the kill fails (`EPIPE`) and is counted, and so is every send until the
  reconnect. So "no `seq` gaps" holds for the clean run (step 2), not across the kill (step 3).
  `itest` case "client through restart" shows the gap: seq 1–4 missing between two STARTs.
- **Directory `fsync`** runs on every `store_open()`, not only when the file is new: a crash
  between creating the file and syncing its directory would otherwise leave a file that looks
  old on the next start, with its name still not on the card.

### Open

- `stored`'s exit 2 (failed write or `fsync`) is covered only at the library level
  (`test_sync_on_broken_handle`); no itest case makes the daemon hit it.
- Nothing stops two `stored`s on the same data file; at M4 `dskyd` is the only launcher. An
  `fcntl` lock in `store_open()` would close it if wanted.
- `DESIGN.md` note on the M3 slice and SEQPACKET being Linux-only (Nick's close-out item).

Commit 3 of 3 is pushed: `1e601a2 M3: progress log and build targets for the storage side`. The storage side (S1–S5) is now pushed and green on Linux, ahead of the Thursday-night target.

The new entry is at the top of [docs/progress-log.md](docs/progress-log.md). It's written for Nick, so he can wire up `tools/run-m3.sh` and the sensor link lines without asking you:
- **Commits and verification:** the three code commits, verified on topeka, which is a CS lab machine, not the Pi. That's stated in the entry.
- **Build targets** as confirmed with him: `build/stored`, `build/dsq`, `STORE_CLIENT_SRC`, `make itest`.
- **How to run it:** a run snippet, `stored`'s arguments and exit codes, its log lines, the 108-byte socket path limit, and how the client behaves.
- **The `kill -9` seq-gap note** for his D demo write-up, plus why the directory fsync runs on every open.
- **Still open:**
  - No itest case makes `stored` itself exit 2.
  - Nothing stops two `stored`s writing the same file.
  - The `DESIGN.md` note on the M3 slice.
  - Your cross-review of his sensor code.

Gates before the commit: `make test` 496 checks, 0 failed; `make itest` 137, 0 failed; `make asan` both suites pass; `make memcheck` 0 errors for both binaries.

**Likely defense questions**
1. *"Your M3 demo shows a seq gap after `kill -9`. Isn't that data loss you should have prevented?"* It's loss we can see and bound, not silent loss. A record in the socket queue is owned by neither side when `stored` dies. Preventing that would need `stored` to send acks and clients to keep and resend unacked records. That makes the sender block or buffer, which breaks the rule that a sensor program never stalls on storage. The gap in `seq` is how the loss is detected.
2. *"Why is `stored`'s sync interval a command-line argument?"* So the test can check the periodic sync in 1 s instead of 60. It's also the knob for evaluation item 10 in `DESIGN.md`, the fsync sweep at 1/10/60/300 s, which can then run without recompiling.
3. *"How does Nick's code depend on yours?"* Only through `store_client.h`, plus the record format both sides already share. The sensor programs link `STORE_CLIENT_SRC` and `src/common/`, not the store library. The socket protocol is one sealed 48-byte record per message, and clients only send.

**Still to do:**
- Integration on `darksky.local`: `make test`, `make memcheck`, `make itest` on the Pi.
- Copying your M3 transcripts into `transcripts/liam/`.
- Your `PROMPTLOG` review of Nick's code.

Write batching (S6) stays off unless you ask for it.
